steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Coat a large baking dish with nonstick cooking spray.
Place corned beef into the prepared baking dish; pour in water. Cover the dish tightly with aluminum foil.
Bake in the preheated oven for 2 hours; drain liquid.
Combine apricot preserves, brown sugar, and soy sauce in a small bowl. Spread evenly over corned beef.
Return to the oven and bake uncovered until meat is tender, 25 to 30 more minutes. Baste occasionally with pan drippings.
Slice corned beef across grain and serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Glazed Corned Beef
raw_recipe.description: This glazed corned beef is cooked in the oven with a sweet sauce of apricot preserves, brown sugar, and soy sauce until tender

review.reviewBody: Last year on St. Pats I made boiled corned beef and this version. The flavor of this recipe was superior to the traditional boiled corned beef, but the baked corned beef was FAR too tough. In prep for this year's St. Pats feast, I tried boiling the corned beef according to the package directions, then draining it, patting it dry, adding the glaze, and baking it for approx 30 minutes (I turned the broiler on for the last couple of minutes to carmelize the top -- watch it carefully though!!) My family agreed it was the best corned beef they had ever tasted. This will be our St. Pats corned beef recipe from now on.

Far superior recipe!!! The sweet glaze against the saltiness of the corned beef is delicious. Typically, I go with the Guinness glaze/onions, etc, but I think I like this better. It's faster to prepare too. The whole family loved it. One thing I noticed is that a standard corned beef that you get at the grocery store is around 2.5lbs. (at least that's the case for Knob Hill). So, you may need to adjust the glaze ingredients by half. In my case, I cooked 2. As most of the other reviewers recommend, I did modify the cooking method, and it turned out perfectly! I rinsed the corned beef, cooked on slow cook mode in my InstantPot with the seasoning packet and a cup of water for 6 hours. That evening, I glazed it and put it in the oven for 25min at 350. It was the perfect consistency. I will definitely make this again.

So glad I found this recipe, not sure why I didn't think to use this method on my corned beef (similar to my ham glaze). I had two beef so I placed each in a 9x13 pyrex with seasoning pack and covered 3/4 with water the baked in oven for 2 hours. 
Drained water then put both roast in one pyrex( meat shrank) Glazed both roast ( used one Tbsp soy only)
I covered with foil and returned back to oven on 275 for 2 more hours. I chose the lower heat and longer method because that is how I make my brisket normally and it is always so tender. 
Delicious result! The sweet glaze did not over power, instead it complemented the saltiness of the corned beef!

I've been looking for a way to make corned beef that doesn't involve beer, was happy to find this. I chose to simmer mine on the stove top for the first part because I wanted it to be tender and moist. It took about 5 hours in my dutch oven, overall this method worked well. Will plan better next time so I can try it in the slow cooker. I had a 3lb brisket so I only mixed a half-recipe, I trimmed the fat before applying the glaze. There was still plenty glaze for my carrots which I par-boiled for 10 mins, then arranged around the meat on a foil-lined baking pan (made potatoes too, but only brushed glaze on the carrots, also sprinkled on some marjoram). Baked at 350 for about 25 minutes, it could have gone just a little longer to caramelize the edges more. The whole meal came out really good, the glaze compliments the corned beef nicely. Thanks for the recipe!

I soak my corned beef in water with the herb packet for atleast 24-36 hours before I intend on cooking it to rid some of the salt, a reverse brine if you will. This recipe taught me the difference in flavor between crock and oven slow cooked. The oven makes a much better flavored meat! I have made this many times, adjusting the time based on the size of the beef, adding flavor to the cooking water with whiskey or herbs, and changing the preserve flavor to complement the other courses. Always use the same ratio as written and always great!

I only modified this slightly in making it for more people (70) so I used increased portions on everything, but didn't change the overall ratios. Also, I used roasters in lieu of an oven and lined the bottom with parchment paper before glazing so it wouldn't stick. This was tender and sweet and my seniors loved it!

Made this by first slow cooking it in the oven with equal parts beer and water. Then drained and added the glaze. Glaze is wonderful. We don't like too much salt, so instead of soy sauce I used 1/4 cup of Cointreau. Works great with the apricot preserves. Husband loved it and declared it a keeper!

5 stars for the glaze, simple and delicious. I scored the fat side then seared both sides in my cast iron pan, then added water and the lid and cooked for 3 hours in the oven before adding glaze for another 30 minutes.

I'm not fond of the typical corned beef & cabbage and came across this recipe. I cooked the corned beef for 4 hours on high in the crockpot according to package directions. I then transferred the corned beef to a baking dish and poured some of the juice from the crockpot into the baking dish. To be honest..when I was preparing the glaze I was skeptical. I couldn't find apricot preserves at the store I shopped at and used peach preserves instead. I cooked in the oven at 350 for 20 minutes basting the corned beef half way thru. THIS WAS AMAZING!! Not too sweet and not too salty!!

This recipe was amazing! I used others reviews and cooked it in a crock pot all day (10 hours) on low. I covered the meat in a wheat beer instead of using water. It was truly amazing. My family loved it and it was SO easy. An easy crock pot meal that will be added to our list of favorites!

I soak my beef over night in a non-reactive pot, it helps to remove more of the excess salt. I then put the beef in a enameled cast iron Dutch oven, add the water, I never bother with the packet that comes with the beef because the beef is already corned (it's actually more for your vegetables), cover and put into a preheated 350 oven, IMMEDIATELY reduce the heat to 250. Bake for 3 hours. The last half hour I drain off the liquid into a double boiler which I will use for steaming my veggies. But before dealing with the veggies, I spread the glaze evenly over the beef and return it back to the oven and increase the oven temp to 350 (uncovered) for about a half hour (watch carefully). Remove from oven and let the beef sit covered on a pre-warmed serving platter on the stove for a half hour. While the beef is "resting" I steam my potatoes and carrots (together) until they are about half done. Add the half done veggies to the pot with the drippings, stir to coat and return the pan to the oven uncovered for about fifteen minutes, check for doneness. Add the potatoes and carrots to the serving platter around the beef and serve.
This is my favorite way to cook corned beef! It has a great flavor and the glaze is an excellent topping. Love this recipe just the way it is!
I’ve made this recipe every year on St. Patrick’s Day for 10 years and it is always a hit!

The only thing I did differently was to put the corned beef on top of uncut carrots to work as a rack when cooking. I took the carrots from under the beef and glazed them along with the beef for the last 25 minutes. Was moist and tender. Love it .
I substituted peach preserves for the apricots. It Turned out good, I did cook of 4hours until tender and used the casserole lid and not aluminum foil.

I love apricot on meats, so we enjoyed it, but I boiled the corned beef, just because it dries out so quickly and was afraid it would be dry/ tough. I also like to instead , mix brown sugar, yellow mustard and ground cloves to taste , sometimes adding in some onion and garlic powder, and cook on cooktop until bubbly. SO incredible on the corned beef AND drizzled on the carrots and potatoes! Yum! Can't wait until 17th! ( This Sunday, or I would make it now! Lol. )
I loved It... Will never make it any other way..... Thanks.....Jvc
This makes a very flavorful corned beef. Even people who may not like corned beef, will love the flavor of this dish!

This was so good. I have made corned beef 100+ times the traditional way. I loved the change and not sure I will ever go back to the traditional corn beef and cabbage recipe. I don’t know why I would not do it this way. Amazing. The only change I made was a minor one me and my husband like spicy food so I used hot pepper jelly.
